lines.text: Seven million American adults have no credit record at all. Another 25 million have one, but no score.
lines.say: Seven million American adults have no credit record at all. Another twenty-five million have one, but no score.

lines.text: No score means worse loan rates, bigger deposits, and more no's.
lines.say: No score means worse loan rates, bigger deposits, and more no's.

lines.text: Today: how to go from zero to a real credit score, step by step, with the actual rules and the math.
lines.say: Today: how to go from zero to a real credit score, step by step, with the actual rules and the math.

lines.text: And the timing is good. FICO's new report says the average score is holding at 714.
lines.say: And the timing is good. FICO's new report says the average score is holding at seven fourteen.

scene.headline: Average U.S. FICO Score holds steady at 714

lines.text: You don't need to be average on day one. You need six months and a plan.
lines.say: You don't need to be average on day one. You need six months and a plan.

lines.text: Chapter one. Why you have no score yet.
lines.say: Chapter one. Why you have no score yet.

lines.text: A credit score is a grade calculated from your credit report. No report, nothing to grade.
lines.say: A credit score is a grade calculated from your credit report. No report, nothing to grade.

lines.text: Your reports are kept by three bureaus: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.
lines.say: Your reports are kept by three bureaus: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.

lines.text: To get a FICO score, you need at least one account that's been open six months or more.
lines.say: To get a FICO score, you need at least one account that's been open six months or more.

lines.text: And at least one account reported to a bureau in the last six months.
lines.say: And at least one account reported to a bureau in the last six months.

lines.text: VantageScore, the other big model, can score you with about one month of history.
lines.say: VantageScore, the other big model, can score you with about one month of history.

lines.text: So the clock starts the day your first account opens. Everything in this video is about starting that clock safely.
lines.say: So the clock starts the day your first account opens. Everything in this video is about starting that clock safely.

lines.text: Here's the recipe the score uses once it exists. FICO publishes the weights.
lines.say: Here's the recipe the score uses once it exists. FICO publishes the weights: payment history thirty-five percent, amounts owed thirty, length of history fifteen, and new credit and mix ten each.

lines.text: Paying on time and keeping balances low are almost two-thirds of it. Remember that. It's the whole game.
lines.say: Paying on time and keeping balances low are almost two-thirds of it. Remember that. It's the whole game.

lines.text: Chapter two. Step one: check your reports for free.
lines.say: Chapter two. Step one: check your reports for free.

lines.text: Before you open anything, see what the bureaus already have on you.
lines.say: Before you open anything, see what the bureaus already have on you.

lines.text: You can pull all three reports free, every week, at AnnualCreditReport dot com. That became permanent in 2023.
lines.say: You can pull all three reports free, every week, at AnnualCreditReport dot com. That became permanent in twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: A report holds four things: who you are, your accounts, who has checked your credit, and certain public records, like bankruptcies.
lines.say: A report holds four things: who you are, your accounts, who has checked your credit, and certain public records, like bankruptcies.

lines.text: Checking your own credit is a soft inquiry. It never hurts your score.
lines.say: Checking your own credit is a soft inquiry. It never hurts your score.

lines.text: Look for accounts you don't recognize. If a thin file has something odd in it, dispute it with the bureau.
lines.say: Look for accounts you don't recognize. If a thin file has something odd in it, dispute it with the bureau.

lines.text: Once you dispute, the bureau gets a thirty-day window to investigate, and it has to fix or remove anything that's wrong or that it can't verify.
lines.say: Once you dispute, the bureau gets a thirty-day window to investigate, and it has to fix or remove anything that's wrong or that it can't verify.

scene.label: Bureau must investigate
scene.sub: Sometimes up to 45 (Fair Credit Reporting Act)

lines.text: If there's truly nothing there, good. You're starting clean.
lines.say: If there's truly nothing there, good. You're starting clean.

lines.text: Chapter three. Step two: pick your first account.
lines.say: Chapter three. Step two: pick your first account.

lines.text: There are four common starter tools. Let's go through each one, with the trade-offs.
lines.say: There are four common starter tools. Let's go through each one, with the trade-offs.

lines.text: Tool one: the secured credit card. You put down a refundable deposit, and that deposit usually becomes your limit.
lines.say: Tool one: the secured credit card. You put down a refundable deposit, and that deposit usually becomes your limit.

lines.text: Deposits often start around 200 dollars. Some issuers take less, like 49 or 99, for a 200 dollar line.
lines.say: Deposits often start around two hundred dollars. Some issuers take less, like forty-nine or ninety-nine, for a two hundred dollar line.

lines.text: It works like a normal card, and it gets reported like one. Check that the issuer reports to all three bureaus.
lines.say: It works like a normal card, and it gets reported like one. Check that the issuer reports to all three bureaus.

lines.text: Tool two: the credit-builder loan. It's a loan backwards.
lines.say: Tool two: the credit-builder loan. It's a loan backwards.

lines.text: The lender locks 300 to 1,000 dollars in a savings account. You pay it off over 6 to 24 months. Then you get the money.
lines.say: The lender locks three hundred to one thousand dollars in a savings account. You pay it off over six to twenty-four months. Then you get the money.

lines.text: The on-time payments get reported. It usually doesn't need a credit check. But interest and fees are a real cost.
lines.say: The on-time payments get reported. It usually doesn't need a credit check. But interest and fees are a real cost.

left.title: Pros
items: Adds a loan to your mix

lines.text: Tool three: become an authorized user on someone else's card, usually a parent or partner.
lines.say: Tool three: become an authorized user on someone else's card, usually a parent or partner.

lines.text: If the issuer reports it, their history can show on your report. But if they pay late, that can show up too.
lines.say: If the issuer reports it, their history can show on your report. But if they pay late, that can show up too.

lines.text: Tool four: a student card or a regular card. Under 21, the law says you need your own income or a cosigner.
lines.say: Tool four: a student card or a regular card. Under twenty-one, the law says you need your own income or a cosigner.

lines.text: You don't need all four. One or two accounts, handled perfectly, is enough to start the clock.
lines.say: You don't need all four. One or two accounts, handled perfectly, is enough to start the clock.

lines.text: And skip applying for five cards at once. Each application is a hard inquiry.
lines.say: And skip applying for five cards at once. Each application is a hard inquiry. It stays on your report two years, and FICO counts it for about one.

scene.label: A hard inquiry stays on your report
scene.sub: FICO counts it for about 1 year

lines.text: Before you apply for a starter card, look for four things.
lines.say: Before you apply for a starter card, look for four things.

lines.text: First, the card reports to all three bureaus. If it doesn't, it can't build your file everywhere.
lines.say: First, the card reports to all three bureaus. If it doesn't, it can't build your file everywhere.

lines.text: Second, a low or no annual fee. On a two hundred dollar limit, a fee eats a big piece of your credit line.
lines.say: Second, a low or no annual fee. On a two hundred dollar limit, a fee eats a big piece of your credit line.

lines.text: Third, a clear path to upgrade to a regular card, so you're not stuck with it forever.
lines.say: Third, a clear path to upgrade to a regular card, so you're not stuck with it forever.

lines.text: And fourth, the deposit comes back, minus anything you still owe, when you upgrade or close the account in good standing.
lines.say: And fourth, the deposit comes back, minus anything you still owe, when you upgrade or close the account in good standing.

lines.text: Many issuers let you prequalify with a soft check first. It's not a guarantee, but you can see your odds without a hard inquiry.
lines.say: Many issuers let you prequalify with a soft check first. It's not a guarantee, but you can see your odds without a hard inquiry.

lines.text: Chapter four. Step three: use it the right way.
lines.say: Chapter four. Step three: use it the right way.

lines.text: Here's the routine. Put one small bill on the card. A streaming plan, a phone bill.
lines.say: Here's the routine. Put one small bill on the card. A streaming plan, a phone bill.

lines.text: Turn on autopay for the full statement balance, so a busy week never becomes a late payment.
lines.say: Turn on autopay for the full statement balance, so a busy week never becomes a late payment.

lines.text: Why it matters: a payment is usually reported late once it's 30 days past due.
lines.say: Why it matters: a payment is usually reported late once it's thirty days past due.

lines.text: And a late payment can stay on your report for up to seven years. On a brand new file, that's brutal.
lines.say: And a late payment can stay on your report for up to seven years. On a brand new file, that's brutal.

lines.text: Next, utilization. That's your balance divided by your limit.
lines.say: Next, utilization. That's your balance divided by your limit.

lines.text: Worked example. Your limit is 200 dollars. You charge 40. 40 divided by 200 is 20 percent.
lines.say: Worked example. Your limit is two hundred dollars. You charge forty. Forty divided by two hundred is twenty percent.

lines.text: Now charge 180 on that same card. That's 90 percent, even though it's only 180 dollars.
lines.say: Now charge one hundred eighty on that same card. That's ninety percent, even though it's only one hundred eighty dollars.

lines.text: Lower is better. A common rule of thumb is staying under 30 percent.
lines.say: Lower is better. A common rule of thumb is staying under thirty percent.

lines.text: Small limits make this tricky. Paying before the statement closes lowers the balance that gets reported.
lines.say: Small limits make this tricky. Paying before the statement closes lowers the balance that gets reported.

lines.text: One more detail: scores look at each card and at your total across all cards. So one maxed-out card can hurt, even if your overall number looks fine.
lines.say: One more detail: scores look at each card and at your total across all cards. So one maxed-out card can hurt, even if your overall number looks fine.

lines.text: Here's what one good month looks like. Your phone bill lands on the card early in the cycle.
lines.say: Here's what one good month looks like. Your phone bill lands on the card early in the cycle.

lines.text: The statement closes, and that small balance is usually what gets reported to the bureaus.
lines.say: The statement closes, and that small balance is usually what gets reported to the bureaus.

lines.text: Then autopay clears the full statement balance before the due date. No interest charged, and one more on-time payment on your record.
lines.say: Then autopay clears the full statement balance before the due date. No interest charged, and one more on-time payment on your record.

lines.text: Now the interest trap. The law says your statement must be delivered at least 21 days before the due date.
lines.say: Now the interest trap. The law says your statement must be delivered at least twenty-one days before the due date.

scene.label: CARD Act: statement arrives at least

lines.text: Pay the full statement balance by then and, on most cards, you pay zero interest.
lines.say: Pay the full statement balance by then and, on most cards, you pay zero interest.

lines.text: Carry a balance, and it gets expensive. Accounts charged interest paid about 22 percent on average this spring.
lines.say: Carry a balance, and it gets expensive. Accounts charged interest paid about twenty-two percent on average this spring.

lines.text: The math: 500 dollars carried at 22 percent a year. 500 times 0.22, divided by 12, is about 9 dollars and 17 cents. In one month.
lines.say: The math: five hundred dollars carried at twenty-two percent a year. Five hundred times zero point two two, divided by twelve, is about nine dollars and seventeen cents. In one month.

lines.text: And carrying a balance doesn't build credit faster. The on-time payment is what counts.
lines.say: And carrying a balance doesn't build credit faster. The on-time payment is what counts.

lines.text: Chapter five. Step four: wait, and watch.
lines.say: Chapter five. Step four: wait, and watch.

lines.text: This part is boring on purpose. Here's the timeline.
lines.say: This part is boring on purpose. Here's the timeline.

lines.text: Around month one, the account shows up on your reports. Some scores, like VantageScore, can appear.
lines.say: Around month one, the account shows up on your reports. Some scores, like VantageScore, can appear.

lines.text: At month six, you meet FICO's minimum. Now you have the score most lenders use.
lines.say: At month six, you meet FICO's minimum. Now you have the score most lenders use.

lines.text: By month twelve, you have a full year of on-time payments. That's the foundation.
lines.say: By month twelve, you have a full year of on-time payments. That's the foundation.

lines.text: Where you land varies. Here's where the country is. The average FICO score, from FICO's own reports.
lines.say: Where you land varies. Here's where the country is. The average FICO score, from FICO's own reports.

lines.text: It bottomed at 686 after the financial crisis, and peaked at 718 in 2023.
lines.say: It bottomed at six eighty-six after the financial crisis, and peaked at seven eighteen in twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: Since then it's slipped a little, partly because missed student loan payments started showing up again in 2025.
lines.say: Since then it's slipped a little, partly because missed student loan payments started showing up again in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: A new file won't hit 714 overnight. Length of history is 15 percent of the score, and only time fixes that.
lines.say: A new file won't hit seven fourteen overnight. Length of history is fifteen percent of the score, and only time fixes that.

lines.text: Watch your progress with free tools, but know the number you see may be a different model than a lender uses.
lines.say: Watch your progress with free tools, but know the number you see may be a different model than a lender uses.

lines.text: Rebuilding after mistakes instead of starting from zero? The same steps work. You're adding new good history on top of the old.
lines.say: Rebuilding after mistakes instead of starting from zero? The same steps work. You're adding new good history on top of the old.

lines.text: Most negative items, like late payments and collections, can stay on your report for seven years. A Chapter 7 bankruptcy can stay for ten.
lines.say: Most negative items, like late payments and collections, can stay on your report for seven years. A Chapter seven bankruptcy can stay for ten.

lines.text: But their weight fades as they age, especially as new on-time payments pile up on top of them.
lines.say: But their weight fades as they age, especially as new on-time payments pile up on top of them.

lines.text: Chapter six. The mistakes that reset the clock.
lines.say: Chapter six. The mistakes that reset the clock.

lines.text: Mistake one: a missed payment. On a thin file, one late payment is a huge share of your history.
lines.say: Mistake one: a missed payment. On a thin file, one late payment is a huge share of your history.

lines.text: Mistake two: maxing out the card, even if you pay it off later. The reported balance is what the score sees.
lines.say: Mistake two: maxing out the card, even if you pay it off later. The reported balance is what the score sees.

lines.text: Mistake three: closing your first card too early. It can shorten your history and cut your total limit.
lines.say: Mistake three: closing your first card too early. It can shorten your history and cut your total limit.

lines.text: Mistake four: applying everywhere at once. More inquiries, and newer accounts drag down your average age.
lines.say: Mistake four: applying everywhere at once. More inquiries, and newer accounts drag down your average age.

lines.text: And a bonus warning: no one can legally remove accurate, current negative info from your report. A company promising that is a red flag.
lines.say: And a bonus warning: no one can legally remove accurate, current negative info from your report. A company promising that is a red flag.

lines.text: What about rent and utility bills? They only help if they're reported to the bureaus, and not every score counts them.
lines.say: What about rent and utility bills? They only help if they're reported to the bureaus, and not every score counts them.

lines.text: Some services report rent for a fee. It's an option to weigh, not a must.
lines.say: Some services report rent for a fee. It's an option to weigh, not a must.

lines.text: Once you have a year or more of clean history, unsecured cards usually become possible.
lines.say: Once you have a year or more of clean history, unsecured cards usually become possible.

lines.text: Many secured cards review you for an upgrade, and you get the deposit back when the account closes or graduates in good standing.
lines.say: Many secured cards review you for an upgrade, and you get the deposit back when the account closes or graduates in good standing.

lines.text: Chapter seven. The one-screen checklist.
lines.say: Chapter seven. The one-screen checklist.

lines.text: Step one. Pull your free reports and fix any errors.
lines.say: Step one. Pull your free reports and fix any errors.

lines.text: Step two. Open one or two starter accounts: a secured card, a credit-builder loan, or authorized user.
lines.say: Step two. Open one or two starter accounts: a secured card, a credit-builder loan, or authorized user.

lines.text: Step three. One small bill, autopay in full, and keep the balance low.
lines.say: Step three. One small bill, autopay in full, and keep the balance low.

lines.text: Step four. Wait. Six months for a FICO score, twelve for a solid first year.
lines.say: Step four. Wait. Six months for a FICO score, twelve for a solid first year.

lines.text: Remember the two numbers that matter most: pay on time, every time, and keep that balance small.
lines.say: Remember the two numbers that matter most: pay on time, every time, and keep that balance small.

lines.text: Credit isn't a talent. It's a record. And a record just takes time and a boring routine.
lines.say: Credit isn't a talent. It's a record. And a record just takes time and a boring routine.

post.ig: No credit score? Here's the 6-month plan to build one from zero.
post.tiktok: Zero credit to a real score: the rules nobody explains.
post.yt_desc:
About 7 million U.S. adults have no credit record and 25 million more have no score. This guide walks through building credit from zero, step by step: checking your free reports, the four starter tools (secured cards, credit-builder loans, authorized user, student cards) and a starter-card checklist, using a card so it helps instead of hurts, and the real timeline to a FICO score, and how rebuilding works. Worked examples show utilization and interest math, plus the mistakes that set you back.

CHAPTERS

Sources: FICO Score Credit Insights report (Aug 25, 2026); FICO average score reports (2017-2025); CFPB credit invisibles update (June 2025); CFPB credit-builder loan research (2020); myFICO scoring criteria; FTC on free weekly credit reports (Oct 2023); Fair Credit Reporting Act; Credit CARD Act of 2009; Federal Reserve G.19 (Q2 2026).

News and education, not financial advice.
